`git` is the helper at `worker.mjs:224`:

const git = (args, opts = {}) =>

# sheepdog — the fleet enforcer marker

Declaring this pack marks a repo as the **fleet enforcer**: the one repo that covers and maintains
every repo under an owner. It's opt-in — a dedicated `sheepdog` repo declares it (it is **not** seeded
by `--init`).

It contributes the pieces only a fleet enforcer needs — three **cross-repo sweeps** — plus their config
schema and the scheduled tasks that run them. The rest of the machinery — running the daily-run (the
orchestrator), the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling — is Claudinite **core**, because
baselining and the daily-run are Claudinite's own responsibility, not the pack's.

**Three sweeps, three questions** — separate, because they close on unrelated conditions. The
**census** ([check-fleet-coverage.mjs](tasks/fleet-census/check-fleet-coverage.mjs)) asks *is this repo a
member* and converges `fleet-adoption` issues. The **freshness sweep**
([check-fleet-freshness.mjs](tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs)) takes coverage as given, asks *is that
membership still meaning anything*, and converges `fleet-drift` issues. The second exists because
per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and removed the last outside look at one:
self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence. The **usage sweep**
([aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs)) asks *what does the fleet
actually use* and writes `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` — a file, not issues, because it reports a
measurement rather than a condition to converge. It exists because a member folds its own skill-usage
numbers and can therefore only say whether a skill loads *there*; whether a skill earns its place at
all is fleet-shaped, and nothing inside a member can see it.

**One manual lever, not a fourth sweep** — [force-fleet-baseline.mjs](fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs)
fires every covered member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` with `overrides: FORCE_TASKS=baselining`,
which is the same button the owner would press in that repo's Actions tab, pressed across the fleet in
one run. It is a **dispatcher, not a maintainer**: each member converges its own mount, with its own
token, under its own delivery policy, and this writes nothing to any member — one queued Actions run
each, and no commit, issue or comment. Under per-project scheduling the fleet needs no push in the
ordinary case; this is for the un-ordinary ones — a canon change the fleet should pick up *now*, or the
tail of members whose next slot is hours away while someone is standing by. A forced run bypasses
baselining's precondition, so a member with nothing to do converges to a cheap no-op: over-using it is
wasteful, never unsafe. A **dormant** member is skipped and reported (it stopped its own scheduler on

enforcer repo is **not**: it is an ordinary member, and leaving it out would make the one repo the owner
is watching the one repo that did not move.

is a scheduled task. Force-baseline answers none and has no cadence: it is owner-initiated, carries its
own inputs (repo filter, dry run, dormant opt-in), and starts when a human presses *Run workflow*. Its

the options for a durable mechanism, are in

`worker.mjs` uses it; force-baseline sits in [fleet-baseline/](fleet-baseline/) beside them, because it
belongs to no task and its runner is the vendored workflow. The pack root holds just what they all

[fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of the entry `config` below).

```json
{ "id": "sheepdog", "config": { "owner": "missingbulb", "kind": "user", "exclude": ["owner/repo-a"],

```

the fleet (a full `owner/name` each) — a repo is kept out by adding it here. `kind: "user"` today; org
support is a later addition. `canonRepo` (default `<owner>/Claudinite`) is what a member's stamped ref
is measured against — named rather than inferred, because a ref tells you nothing about where it came
from. `staleDays` (default `14`) is how far behind is too far. Both are freshness-only and both
default, so an existing sheepdog config keeps working untouched.

*implementation* — an account-spanning PAT — happens to scan every repo under the owner, but their
declaration, scheduling, and lifecycle are exactly those of any pack task. None declares the
`fleet` signal nor `session_scope: fleet`; the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in
how a task is wired. (The task files carry the same note.)

[`fleet-freshness`](tasks/fleet-freshness/task.md) (`weekly`) and
[`fleet-usage`](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (`daily`) scheduled tasks, all `agent_model: none`, each
with its sweep as `agent_preprocessing`. The first two are `expected_outcome: none` (they open
**issues**, never a PR); the usage sweep is `merged-pr`, because its output IS a tracked file and an
auto-merging PR keeps that write inside the outcome taxonomy, lets this repo's CI gate a malformed
file, and makes the daily PR stream a browsable audit trail. Freshness is weekly because drift is
measured in days — a daily sweep would re-ask a question whose answer cannot have changed; usage is
daily because the members fold daily. There is **no coverage workflow** — preprocessing
runs Action-side inside this repo's one scheduler workflow, so the repo Actions secret is already
reachable there; each task's `required_secrets: ['FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN']` stamps the name into that
workflow's env and is what asks the owner for it (a fine-grained PAT spanning the owner's repos:
Metadata + Contents read, Issues read/write, and Contents write on this repo for baseline-migration
retirement — freshness adds no scope). A workflow that exists only to hold a secret is redundant
([packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md](../basics/scheduled-tasks.md)) — the force-baseline workflow above is
not that: it exists because the operation is manual, and it reads the same secret only incidentally.

repositories to that PAT. Dispatching another repo's workflow is an Actions *write*, so a token scoped
for the three read-only sweeps answers `403` on every member. The sweep reports that per repo as
`no-permission` and fails the run rather than retrying: it is a grant to fix once, not a transient. The
sweeps themselves are unaffected — they never dispatch anything.

**What freshness assumes** — baselining reverts a stamp-only bump, so `claudinite.updated` advances
only when canon changed that member's vendor set. Age of the **stamped ref** is therefore the honest
liveness measure, and `behind` reads *"has not picked canon up in `staleDays`"*, not *"canon moved"*.
A member whose vendor set genuinely saw no change in the window is the one false positive; `staleDays`
is the knob, and the drift issue says so.

**When they fail** — a repo the census cannot classify is `unknown`, never uncovered, and a member the
freshness sweep cannot probe is `unknown`, never behind: no issue opened, no open issue closed on its
behalf, and a non-zero exit. A non-zero preprocessing subprocess fails the task, and the scheduler
converges one open `needs-human` issue for it.

# sheepdog

The fleet **enforcer** marker — declaring it makes a repo the one that covers and maintains every repo
under an owner. Opt-in (a dedicated sheepdog repo declares it; **not** seeded by `--init`). It
standardizes the fleet coverage that used to be bespoke Claudinite infrastructure into a declaration.

Thin by design: prose + the config schema (the sheepdog pack entry's `config` = `{ owner, kind, exclude,
canonRepo, staleDays }`) + three cross-repo **sweeps**, each with the one agentless scheduled task that
runs it (the sweep is its `agent_preprocessing`; no workflow of its own) — plus one **manual lever**
that has no cadence and therefore does have a workflow:

| sweep | task | asks |
|---|---|---|
| [check-fleet-coverage.mjs](tasks/fleet-census/check-fleet-coverage.mjs) | [fleet-census](tasks/fleet-census/task.md) (daily) | is this repo a **member**? → adoption issues |
| [check-fleet-freshness.mjs](tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs) | [fleet-freshness](tasks/fleet-freshness/task.md) (weekly) | is a member **keeping up**? → drift issues |
| [aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs) | [fleet-usage](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (daily) | what does the fleet **actually use**? → `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` |
| [force-fleet-baseline.mjs](fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs) | *(no task — the [fleet-baseline workflow](stubs/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml), `workflow_dispatch` only)* | make every member baseline **now** → one queued run per member |

The second exists because per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and, in doing so,
removed the last thing that looked at a member from the **outside** — self-maintenance cannot detect its
own absence. The third exists for the same shape of reason one rung up: a member can say whether a
skill loads *there*, and only a view across every member can say whether it earns its place at all.

A member that declares itself **dormant** (`"dormant": true` in its own declaration) is out of the
freshness sweep and out of the usage denominator — its scheduler is stopped, so its mount falls
behind by design and its silence says nothing about any skill. It stays a **member**: the census
is unchanged, because dormancy is about upkeep, not membership.

The fourth is not a sweep and not a task: **force-baseline** answers no recurring question, so it has
no cadence to schedule. It is the owner pressing *Run workflow* — fire every member's own scheduler
with `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` so the fleet picks canon up now instead of over the next day. It takes a
repo filter, a dry run, and an opt-in for dormant members; it writes nothing to any member (one queued

vendored scheduler stays the enforcer's only one — and because GitHub reads workflows solely from a
repo's own `.github/`, the enforcer carries a byte-identical copy of the stub there, **landed by a
session** and synced by nothing: the nightly converge pushes with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which can
never write under `.github/workflows/` ([#649](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/649)).
Edit the pack, then land the copy.

lives in [fleet-baseline/](fleet-baseline/) beside them, because it belongs to no task. Only what they
all share sits at the pack root: [fleet-api.mjs](fleet-api.mjs) (the cross-repo REST primitives) and
[fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of this pack's entry `config`).

The rest of the machinery — running the daily-run, the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling —
is Claudinite **core**. Carries no conformance checks. Policy + config: [RULES.md](RULES.md).

name: Fleet baseline

# THE ENFORCER'S MANUAL LEVER over the whole fleet: force every covered member to
# baseline NOW, instead of waiting for each one's next hourly slot. It fires each
# member's OWN scheduler workflow with `overrides: FORCE_TASKS=baselining` — the same
# button the owner would press in that repo's Actions tab, pressed across the fleet in
# one run. Nothing is baselined here: each member converges its own mount, with its own
# token, under its own delivery policy.
#
# A MANAGED COPY, LANDED BY HAND. This file is owned by the sheepdog pack
# (packs/sheepdog/stubs/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml); the copy here is byte-identical
# and carries no repo-specific value. It lives in .github/ rather than running from the
# mount because GitHub reads workflows only from a repo's own .github/; the LOGIC it
# runs stays in the mount (.claudinite/shared/packs/sheepdog/fleet-baseline/), so this
# file is copy-verbatim in every enforcer repo and changes only when its inputs change.
#
# NOTHING SYNCS IT, and nothing can: baselining's converge pushes with the Action's
# GITHUB_TOKEN, which GitHub never permits to create or update a file under
# .github/workflows/ (there is no `permissions:` key that grants it), and a rejected
# push fails the WHOLE converge — one unpushable file wedges the member's every other
# update too (#649). So a change to the pack stub reaches here the same way this file
# first did: a session PR, using credentials that hold the `workflows` permission.
# Fix the pack, then land the copy — and until you do, this file is stale, not managed.
#
# NO `schedule:` TRIGGER, DELIBERATELY. The vendored `claudinite-scheduler.yml` is this
# repo's only cron (packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md), and this workflow does not add a
# second one. It is not recurring work with a cadence — it is an owner-initiated
# operation, started by a human pressing "Run workflow", which is exactly what
# workflow_dispatch is for. Members baseline themselves hourly; this is for the cases
# that should not wait for that.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      repos:
        description: 'Limit to these repos (comma-separated; bare name or owner/name). Empty = every covered member.'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dry_run:
        description: 'List what would be dispatched without dispatching anything.'
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false
      include_dormant:
        description: 'Also force members that declared themselves dormant (they are skipped by default — a dormant repo stopped its own scheduler on purpose).'
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

# One fleet-wide force at a time. Not cancel-in-progress: a run that has already
# dispatched half the fleet has done half its work for real, and killing it would leave
# the fleet in a state no report describes.
concurrency:
  group: fleet-baseline
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Reads this repo's own declaration for the sheepdog config; every write it makes is to
# ANOTHER repo's Actions, over FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN, which github.token cannot do.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  force-baseline:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Force baselining across the fleet
        env:
          # The account-spanning PAT the sheepdog sweeps already use, plus ONE scope they
          # do not need: Actions READ AND WRITE on the owner's repositories. Dispatching
          # another repo's workflow is an Actions write; without it every member reports
          # `no-permission` and the run fails.
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          FLEET_BASELINE_REPOS: ${{ inputs.repos }}
          FLEET_BASELINE_DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
          FLEET_BASELINE_INCLUDE_DORMANT: ${{ inputs.include_dormant }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/packs/sheepdog/fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs

input.body:
Makes the fleet-baseline workflow arrive on Sheepdog **automatically**, by fixing the delivery gap underneath it rather than hand-landing the file (missingbulb/Sheepdog#67 is closed unmerged).

## The problem, precisely

`deliver()` pushes with the Action's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`worker.mjs:429` → the `execFileSync` helper at `worker.mjs:224`). GitHub never permits that token to create *or update* anything under `.github/workflows/`, and the refusal is **remote-side and rejects the whole ref**:

```
! [remote rejected] HEAD -> claudinite/maintenance-2026-08-05-3fa950
(refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow ... without `workflows` permission)
```

So one undeliverable file didn't merely fail to land — it took the mount convergence, the wiring, and every other migration note down with it, on **every** run, because the converge is idempotent and re-attempted it identically each cycle.

## The fix

The converge now **withholds** those paths from its commit (`withheldWorkflowPaths`), pushes everything else, and escalates to the **agent stage**, whose writes go through MCP — a credential that *does* hold the `workflows` permission.

Nothing is handed to the agent directly: the branch is the whole handoff, and the agent rediscovers the work by re-running the same mechanical apply in its own checkout, so agent-preprocessing DESIGN §3's "no code→agent data channel" is untouched (task.md §2b). A converge whose *only* content was a workflow file still cuts its branch and PR via an empty commit — that's where the agent does its half.

**This is not a sheepdog concern.** `convergeWiring` writes `claudinite-scheduler.yml` itself, so a change to the scheduler stub was latently this same wedge on every member in the fleet. It now rides the same path.

With delivery possible, the `sheepdog-fleet-baseline` record returns unchanged from its first form. Nothing about the record was ever wrong — the path underneath it didn't exist yet.

## Verification

- `node --test` over the CI test roots: **1161 pass, 0 fail**
- New tests **seen to fail**: mutating the prefix and dropping the escalation branch produces 3 failures; restored, 48/48 in that file
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking**, 9 advisory (pre-existing `engine/` file-placement notes)
- `node migrations/apply.mjs` on canon: still a no-op — the record's `appliesTo` gate holds, canon doesn't declare sheepdog

## What to watch on the first real run

The agent stage's MCP credential is assumed to carry the `workflows` permission — verified by hand in this session (that's how Sheepdog#67's file was pushed), but not yet by an unattended executor run. If it doesn't, the file stays unlanded and the converge still succeeds — the failure mode is now "not yet delivered" instead of "everything wedged".

Refs #649

Comment class: other (question)

Three answers, and I need to correct your first one on two points.

**1. Not all of `.github` — only `.github/workflows/`.** The withhold set is exactly that prefix (`UNPUSHABLE_PREFIX`, `worker.mjs`). Everything else under `.github/` pushes normally with the Action token: `.github/actions/**` (composite actions — the `chrome-release-vendoring` record materializes three of them and always pushed fine), `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `dependabot.yml`, `CODEOWNERS`. GitHub's rule is about *workflow files* specifically, not the directory. One of my tests pins that distinction (`.github/actions/report-failure/action.yml` stays pushable).

Also a wording fix: it triggers **baselining's own agent stage**, not a separate "migration agent". Same task, second stage — the executor session picks up the dispatch issue and continues on the branch preprocessing already pushed.

**2. `.claude/` — no, nothing special.** To GitHub it's an ordinary directory; hooks, settings, and skills there push with the Action token like any other file. That's why the wiring converge has always been able to write `.claude/settings.json` (it's one of `convergeWiring`'s four surfaces) without ever hitting this.

**3. The other `GITHUB_TOKEN` limits.** Splitting these by how much I'd stake on them:

*Documented in this repo, load-bearing, learned the hard way:*
- **Its pushes and PR-creations don't start workflows** — GitHub's recursion guard. This one has three issue numbers on it (#565, #455, #432) and is why `deliver()` explicitly dispatches the maintenance PR's checks itself. `workflow_dispatch`/`repository_dispatch` are the documented exceptions. (`git-github-advanced` SKILL.md:76, `worker.mjs:162`.)
- **Cannot write workflow files** — the one you just hit.
- **Single-repo scope.** It sees only the repo running the workflow, which is the entire reason `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` exists for the sheepdog sweeps.

*Confident, not written down here:* it expires at job end (24h max); on a `pull_request` from a fork it's read-only with no secrets; the repo's "Workflow permissions" setting can cap it read-only by default regardless of what a workflow's `permissions:` block asks for.

*Would want to verify before relying on it:* whether it can submit an approving PR review (I believe it's blocked, but I haven't tested it), and how branch-protection exemptions apply to it. I'd rather check than assert.

I didn't broaden the withhold set beyond workflow files deliberately — withholding a path that *is* pushable would route work to the agent that the converge could have done itself, trading a deterministic write for an agentic one.
